releaseScope.reason: Private-beta retention, commercial approval, remote reliability, legal, security-review, and recovery evidence do not exist.

findings.title: Real authentication and onboarding
findings.rationale: Live-mode authentication, verification, recovery, session revocation, and transactional onboarding are implemented and tested locally. Registration supports closed, invite_only, and public modes; invite_only is the current production-shaped default, while production startup and release authorization reject public admission until its separate gates pass.

evidence.detail: Production permits closed or invite_only registration and rejects public admission.

findings.title: Server-derived tenant authorization
findings.rationale: Protected Web routes and live API requests derive access from durable membership and fail closed in tenant tests.

findings.title: Canonical server state for release-scope workflows
findings.rationale: The founder operating loop and collaboration live paths use typed server repositories; browser storage is limited to preferences and recoverable drafts.

evidence.detail: Implemented live workflow boundary and verification summary.

findings.title: Durable PostgreSQL repositories
findings.rationale: Tenant-scoped repositories, concurrency, idempotency, transactions, audit, and outbox behavior are covered by PostgreSQL integration tests.

findings.title: Complete production deployment topology
findings.rationale: Only a self-signed local/CI topology exists. No managed remote staging or production Web/API/worker/PostgreSQL runtime is provisioned.

evidence.detail: Current deployment truth and missing remote services.
Local production-shaped topology using test transport allowances.

findings.title: Persistent and authorized Teams and Messages
findings.rationale: Teams, Team rooms, messages, participants, retention, and invalidation use durable authorization-aware live paths.

findings.title: Private service-worker cache safety
findings.rationale: Private app documents and API responses are excluded from shared service-worker caching.

findings.title: Truthful capability and effect labeling
findings.rationale: Unsupported durable, provider, billing, import, file, and automation effects are disabled or explicitly labeled.

findings.title: Production-like CI and deployed topology validation
findings.rationale: CI is configured to enforce formatting, route/asset budgets, Chromium/WebKit browser gates, live identity, migrations, and a production-shaped topology whose Web, two APIs, and two Workers report one candidate release ID/full Git SHA and their actual Docker image IDs. Those new workflow changes have not run remotely, API/worker/migration still use NODE_ENV=test transport allowances in CI, and no operated remote environment is exercised. Production manifest authorization also requires external evidence-content and completed-authorization verifiers that the repository CLI deliberately does not provide. Verified records must match registered per-kind schemas, satisfy substantive thresholds/checks, reconcile derived metrics, and bind candidate artifact identity; no trusted release controller is deployed.

evidence.detail: Configured format, performance, multi-browser, live-mode, and topology gates.
Fail-closed external evidence and authorization verification boundary.
Configured per-instance release and image correlation smoke.

findings.title: Implementation-status documentation truth
findings.rationale: Repository documentation consistently labels the hosted experience and undeployed live runtime limitations.

findings.title: Safe public route and indexing behavior
findings.rationale: The preview is noindexed, canonical URLs are validated, and sensitive routes use no-store/noindex headers. Public-beta indexing remains a separate launch decision.

evidence.detail: Sensitive route cache and indexing headers.

findings.title: Operable worker and outbox lifecycle
findings.rationale: Leasing, retry, dead-letter state, metrics, and shutdown are implemented, but no deployed supervision or reviewed dead-letter inspect/redrive procedure exists.

evidence.detail: Implemented worker boundary and missing operator controls.

findings.title: Production integrations, files, imports, and scalable search
findings.rationale: Providers, private files, and real import remain disabled without pilot evidence. PostgreSQL search applies tenant and accessible-Workspace predicates before LIMIT, and a local integration harness covers 100 Workspaces/10,000 items. Full-text/trigram indexing and deployed performance evidence remain absent.

evidence.detail: Permission predicates are applied before result limits.

findings.title: Approved and exercised billing lifecycle
findings.rationale: There is no approved price, provider, checkout, portal, webhook processing, invoice, dunning, cancellation, downgrade, or refund implementation.

findings.title: Reviewed legal package and executable privacy lifecycle
findings.rationale: Privacy and terms are previews; export, deletion, revocation, retention enforcement, deletion-safe evidence, and post-membership DSAR access are absent.

evidence.detail: Pending legal, DPA, region, and processor review.

findings.title: Active production telemetry, request protection, and browser policy
findings.rationale: Bounded local RUM ingestion and normalized route reporting are configured, alongside runtime controls and vendor-neutral observability assets. No production collector, pager, error tracker, source maps, staffed ownership, measured RUM window, or nonce/hash enforcing CSP is active.

evidence.detail: Bounded local Web Vitals ingestion into structured logs.

findings.title: Complete live-data and recovery state coverage
findings.rationale: The golden loop and collaboration have strong state handling, but every release-scope route/state and cross-browser recovery matrix is not yet recorded.

findings.title: Exercised release, restore, and incident controls
findings.rationale: No managed backup/PITR restore, migration rollback, remote incident, alert-routing, or provider failure exercise has produced evidence.

evidence.detail: Restore policy and drill are explicitly unprovisioned.
Release ordering exists without exercised remote promotion.

findings.title: Native mobile and desktop parity
findings.rationale: Web/PWA-only is the accepted GA scope. Mobile and desktop remain non-distributed companion foundations and must be labeled accordingly; any later native release requires a new reviewed gate.

findings.title: Complete German localization
findings.rationale: English-only is the accepted GA scope. German controls and claims must remain absent until complete extraction, persistence, translation, and responsive QA pass under a new reviewed gate.

findings.title: Founder-loop scope discipline
findings.rationale: Release scope is the founder operating loop plus contextual Teams/Messages. CRM, full chat/email, accounting, payroll, advanced Gantt, and native parity are excluded.

findings.title: Enforced performance and reference-volume budgets
findings.rationale: Route/asset budgets and bounded RUM ingestion are configured, and a PostgreSQL search harness covers 100 Workspaces/10,000 items with permission filtering before LIMIT. The new CI budget gate has not run remotely; production RUM, representative mobile Core Web Vitals, Portfolio/browser reference-volume evidence, and measured query plans remain absent, so this deferral still blocks GA authorization.

evidence.detail: Directional local evidence and missing production gate.

findings.title: Complete WCAG A/AA and assistive-technology evidence
findings.rationale: Axe is configured to fail all reported in-scope WCAG A/AA findings across Chromium, WebKit, and mobile Chromium projects. Local Chromium and WebKit executions produced separate exact, owned, expiring demo/live incomplete-result inventories; no violation is accepted. The new CI workflow has not run remotely, and recorded keyboard/screen-reader/200%-zoom/reduced-motion/high-contrast/touch evidence remains incomplete.

evidence.detail: Configured full in-scope WCAG A/AA assertions.
Manual checks without completed release record.
Configured Chromium, WebKit, and mobile Chromium projects.

findings.title: Repository formatting gate
findings.rationale: The repository formatting baseline is normalized and format:check is configured as a required quality-job step. Remote workflow execution is still tracked by P0-09 rather than reopening this configuration finding.

evidence.detail: Formatting is configured before contracts and builds.

findings.title: Long-lived branch CI coverage
findings.rationale: CI now runs on every pushed branch and every pull request.

findings.title: Pinned dependency support ranges
findings.rationale: Many package declarations still use latest and no controlled update automation is configured.

findings.title: Immutable GitHub Action references
findings.rationale: Actions use moving major tags rather than reviewed commit SHAs.

findings.title: Coverage and client release tests
findings.rationale: Web browser suites are configured and have executed locally for Chromium, WebKit, and mobile Chromium, but the new remote run has not occurred, no risk-based coverage threshold is enforced, and excluded native clients have no distributable release smoke evidence.

evidence.detail: Current test scripts have no coverage gate.

findings.title: API mutable test-state isolation
findings.rationale: Live-mode tests use injected PostgreSQL repositories and isolated database fixtures rather than process-global product maps.

findings.title: Internal founderhq naming
findings.rationale: Internal package/database names remain non-public implementation details and must be migrated before any public SDK or developer platform.

evidence.detail: Public release boundary remains Web/PWA product, not SDK.
